text:
Sam: quick note — after the midnight canary i pulled profiling for the 512-token p99 regression. looks like coalesce jitter + microwindow alignment is amplifying kernel-switch overheads.
Anya: ugh, saw that on the dashboard. perfbot alerted a +18% p99, right?
PerfBot: alert: p99 latency +18% for model=redwood-v3-qa config=dyn-coal-std, traffic=5rps, window=3-9ms. trace id=cb-sweep-42
Sam: exact. raw flame shows repeated tiny kernel invocations (~2-4ms) separated by 0.6-1.2ms waits — KV cache priming is misaligned with coalesce boundary.
Kevin: are you seeing token-budget thrashing? if microbatches are forming with variable size, kernel selection flips between cu-attn and fallback path.
Sam: yes — sequence: small microbatch hits cu-attn optimized path, next arrival changes batch size & triggers q8 fallback. overhead ~= 0.8-1.0ms per switch. multiplied by repeated small windows => p99 spike.
Anya: proposed experiment: add deterministic splay to microwindow start times (splay=0.8ms) + raise jitter-floor to 1.0ms and lower max-coalesce to 6ms. run for 2h on canary.
Ida: also add KV cache write-back delay of 1.5ms to avoid priming during the microwindow boundary. we should instrument KV hit/miss per batch.
Sam: plan: implement three variants — A) base (current), B) splay-floor (splay 0.8ms + jitter-floor 1.0ms), C) splay-stagger (random splay 0.5-1.5ms + kv-delay 1.5ms). collect: per-request kernel-switch count, batch-size distribution, kv-hit-rate, p50/p95/p99.
Kevin: make sure to tag traces with kernel_id and batch_epoch. add a histogram for inter-kernel gap.
Anya: i'll spin the canary and set traffic weight 10% -> 30% over 30m ramp. will push lightweight build with debug flags.
PerfBot: metric snapshot (pre-change): p50=28ms p95=82ms p99=185ms, kernel_switch_rate=0.27/small-batch.
Sam: expected outcome: B should reduce switch churn and bring p99 down ~10-12% if kv-priming alignment is main culprit; C expected to reduce worst-case but might slightly increase median due to stagger.
Ida: thumbs up. can we add a cheap on-host profiler for microburst detection (sample every 100ms)? if we see >3 kernel switches per burst we rollback.
Anya: added. launching A/B/C canary now. will post initial 30m summary. :rocket:
Kevin: if B looks good, we should backport splay-floor to dedicated runtime default and add an opt-in for splay-stagger for bursty tenants.
Sam: logging note: include kernel selection reason code (size, dtype, quant) in trace so we can correlate decisions.
PerfBot: update: 30m into run — variant B p99 down 11%, kernel_switch_rate -46%, kv-hit-rate +6%.
Anya: nice — initial numbers promising. i'll let it run the full 2h then publish perf diff and config patch for review.
Kevin: also capture example trace where a single request saw 4 switches — send to #eng-runtime with trace id.
Sam: will attach. thanks all.
Anya: follow-up: saving raw traces to s3://cb-sweep/1767777777/ for offline flame analysis.
Ida: after full run, schedule a quick postmortem with the runtime kernel team to decide default heuristics.
Sam: agreed. next update in ~90m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
